blocks.content: Indian Railways was nationalized in 1951 and remains the backbone of domestic freight and passenger transportation across India.

rows: Mainline passenger and heavy freight corridors
Secondary regional routes (under conversion via Project Unigauge)
Mountain railways and heritage routes (e.g., Toy Trains)

items: Remember committee names: Acworth Committee (1920–21) recommended Railway Budget separation; Bibek Debroy Committee (2015) recommended its merger.
Shree Siddharoodha Swamiji Hubballi Station in Karnataka holds the record for the world's longest railway platform (1,507 meters).
The Chenab Rail Bridge in Jammu & Kashmir is the highest railway bridge in the world, standing 359 meters above the river bed.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The first passenger train in India operated between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane on April 16, 1853, covering a distance of 34 km.
Indian Railways was nationalized in 1951 and is currently structured into 19 operational administrative zones.
The Railway Budget was separated from the General Budget in 1924 following the Acworth Committee recommendations and merged back in 2017 based on the Bibek Debroy Committee report.
Project Unigauge was initiated in 1992 to standardize track metrics by converting metre and narrow gauges into broad gauge.
